title: Routing & Fallback Policy Simulator + Rollback Synthesizer for Variant Deployments
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build a standalone simulation harness and policy synthesizer that evaluates deployment routing & fallback rules for model variant rollouts across regions and capacity tiers. The simulator will: (1) run synthetic multi-region traffic with configurable latency/capacity distributions; (2) validate compatibility scoring (model variant semantic/IO compatibility and KV cache warmability); (3) exercise tier-aware admission control and spillback; (4) produce automated rollback signatures (rollback synthesizer) based on quantile SLA breaches, error modes, and quality regressions from canary probes. The goal is to reduce manual rollouts, shorten mean-time-to-detect, and prevent region-wide degradations during progressive deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can replay archived traffic traces across 3 simulated regions with configurable capacity tiers
Policy synthesizer outputs deterministic routing decisions given identical inputs and produces fallthrough lanes for partial compatibility
Rollback synthesizer emits human-readable rollback rationale (metrics + observable signatures) and a confidence score
End-to-end test demonstrates automated circuit-breaker-triggered spillback from premium tier to standard tier without request loss in > 95% of trials
Bench: simulator can run a 1M request canary matrix (10 variants x 10 traffic slices) in < 30 minutes on CI runner
notes: Motivation: current rollouts rely on ad-hoc scripts and manual judgement when regions or tiers saturate. We need a repeatable decision-making model to avoid cascading fallbacks.
Key deliverables: simulation harness (go/python), policy synthesizer library (rust/go), rollback signature registry, and test-suite integrated with GH actions.
Trade-offs: full fidelity (simulating GPU scheduling + kernel selection) is expensive; initial phase will use probabilistic cost/latency models derived from recent telemetry.
Compatibility heuristics: semantic compatibility score + KV-warmability score + stateful session affinity penalty. These are additive with tunable thresholds per customer tier.
Cost modeling: include per-token latency/cost delta in simulations to quantify economic impact of spillbacks/quantization fallbacks.
implementation_plan: Week 1: prototype harness that replays existing trace samples and a simple router emulator
Week 2: implement compatibility scoring and spillback heuristics; add region latency distributions
Week 3: build rollback synthesizer rules engine + mapping to human rationale templates
Week 4: integrate canary metric probes (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, quality delta) and run stress matrix
Week 5: run validation against historical rollout incidents and refine thresholds
Week 6: merge library, create GH action, and draft runbook for on-call and SRE
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring functions (semantic, kv-warmability, affinity)
Integration test: multi-region replay with induced capacity loss in one region
Regression test: run historical incident trace and expect rollback_synthesizer to match known remediation
Chaos experiment: randomly drop 10% of premium tier nodes to verify spillback stability
risks_mitigation: Risk: simulator divergence from production scheduler. Mitigation: calibrate with telemetry and sample live experiments behind feature flag.
Risk: false positive rollbacks (too-sensitive rules). Mitigation: conservative default thresholds + require multi-metric corroboration.
Risk: long CI times. Mitigation: provide fast smoke mode with smaller sample sizes and a full mode gated to nightly runs.
